title: Stack space of recursive calls
summary: Stack space depends on how many calls remain active at once, as each nested recursive call adds a stack frame.
context: Here n is a positive integer, counted below under standard execution without tail-call optimization.
result: Each level uses constant local space, and at maximum depth n levels coexist simultaneously for O(n) peak stack space; releasing frames afterward one by one does not reduce the peak already reached.

frames.title: Stack space of recursive calls
frames.explanation: The left column, "Recurse downward", steps down by 1 from linear_recur(n) to the base case linear_recur(1), spanned by a brace labeled "Recursion depth n". Because outer calls wait for inner calls to finish, n stack frames coexist at the deepest point; control then unwinds up the right column, "Return upward", freeing each level's stack frame only as it returns. Although the right column writes return 0 whereas the current Python code uses a bare return (returning None), that difference does not affect the stack-space count.
